// purpose: Extension-host project of debug-generator: the Node side of this workspace. src/webview/** runs in the webview iframe and is the program of tsconfig.webview.json, which keeps DOM globals out of host code and Node globals out of the webview. `tsc -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.webview.json` builds both, and the root solution references both.
// format: Strict JSON, so notes are top-level `"// …"` keys, which TypeScript ignores; inside `compilerOptions` such a key is an error (TS5023).
// compilerOptions.emit: `composite` with declaration-only emit into the base's `${configDir}/.tsbuild` paths; tsconfig.webview.json moves its output and stamp to .tsbuild/webview, so the two projects never share either. tsc never writes dist/: esbuild.mjs and `vite build` own it, and the VSIX ships it.
// compilerOptions.rootDir: "." because the inputs span src/, test/ and vite.config.ts; "src" would reject the last two (TS6059).
// compilerOptions.lib: ES2023 only, the base's set restated so the host boundary is explicit: `window`, `document` and the other DOM globals do not type-check in host code. `lib` replaces the inherited array, so the webview project names ES2023 again beside DOM.
// compilerOptions.types: "node" and "vscode". @types/node is a root devDependency; do not add it to this manifest. @types/vscode 1.125.0 matches the `engines.vscode` floor, so no API newer than the oldest supported editor type-checks.
// compilerOptions.types.not-listed.moch: "mocha" is not listed: @types/mocha is not a dependency of this workspace, and the copy inside @vscode/test-cli is unreachable from `types` (TS2688). Instead, each suite under test/suite/*.test.ts declares the Mocha globals it uses (`describe`, `it`, `before`, `after`, `beforeEach`, `afterEach`) locally, with module-scoped `declare function` statements.
// compilerOptions.module: `module`/`moduleResolution` are not overridden: sources are authored as ESM under bundler resolution, and esbuild.mjs emits the CommonJS bundle VS Code loads (package.json has no "type": "module"). NodeNext would make these files CommonJS, where `import`/`export` syntax fails under the inherited `verbatimModuleSyntax`. Relative specifiers are extensionless. Keep `await` inside functions: esbuild cannot lower top-level `await` into a CommonJS bundle.
// compilerOptions.not-set: No `paths`/`baseUrl`: workspace packages resolve through the pnpm symlink and each package's `exports` map. esbuild follows its runtime conditions into dist/; tsc follows its source-first `types` condition to src/ (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3).
// include: src/**/*.ts (host modules and their colocated Vitest suites), test/**/*.ts (the @vscode/test-cli suites, type-checked here, bundled by esbuild.mjs and run in a real editor rather than by Vitest) and vite.config.ts. esbuild.mjs and .vscode-test.mjs are plain ESM: linted, never compiled.
// exclude: `exclude` replaces the base list, so dist, .tsbuild and node_modules are repeated. src/webview/** belongs to the webview project alone. src/webview-messages.ts is deliberately in both projects: it is the environment-neutral message union both halves import, and each project emits it into its own directory, so do not relocate or duplicate it. test/fixtures/** is a workspace the suites open at runtime, not program input; .vscode-test is @vscode/test-electron's working directory.
// references: shared and protocol only; they order the build, and `tsc -b` type-checks this program against their .tsbuild declarations, so `pnpm typecheck` never reads a stale dist/. panel-renderer belongs to the webview project. No apps/* reference: esbuild.mjs bundles the local service outside the type system, and the host reaches it over HTTP and WebSocket through @debuggen/protocol.
